- When sentiment shows strong negative signals (e.g., -0.33 or 0.00) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 65+), model often overshoots downward — apply a “cool-down” buffer to prevent premature reversal.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., 1.00) and price is falling, model underestimates the drop — adjust downward bias by 2–3% of recent range.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if price is above 60 for 3+ days, forecast should not rise above 62 unless sentiment confirms strong bullish momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates downside risk — add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture volatility clustering — apply smoothing filter to avoid overfitting to recent trends.
